title: Chain config shape (v8 item (b), deep-research-v8-directional-followup-2026-09-15.md §2.4(c))
description: Validates the real top-level fields `src/chain.js` and `src/chain-lint.js` actually read (derived by grepping `config.<field>` across src/chain.js, not copied from one example chain file - so this covers mock chains and compliance chains too, not just the coder-gate/plan-debate shapes). Precedent and style: config/seat-model-schema.json (draft-07, one $id, descriptive `description` fields explaining why a shape is allowed, not just what it is). additionalProperties is false at the top level, so an unrecognized/typo'd top-level key fails loud here (chain-lint.js has no equivalent check - its rule 1 only validates seats.* sub-keys). Deliberately permissive at the leaves this repo's own chain-lint.js already validates at runtime with better, config-specific error messages (challenge, allocator, compliance, roster) - duplicating that validation here would drift from chain-lint.js's real rules the first time either changes; this schema's job is catching the shape errors chain-lint.js does NOT check (typos in top-level key names, wrong types, an unrecognized field), which is exactly where config drift has actually gone unnoticed (test/landing-page.test.js's own precedent: a page shipped a stale count nobody caught until a derived test existed).

^_.description: A leading-underscore top-level key is a free-form human note, not engine-read config - real precedent: archive/chains/gp-judge-v1.json's "_maxTokensNote". Left unconstrained in type/shape on purpose (it's prose, not data any code parses) rather than special-cased to one exact field name, so the next author adding a similarly-named note doesn't retrigger this exact validation failure.

name.description: Chain identifier, matches the filename stem by convention (not enforced here - test/chain-schema.test.js checks structural validity, not naming).

resumeAfterStop.description: Whether a run of this chain that was stopped before finishing (exit 18: a person, a client cancel or a wall clock) may be continued with --resume or resume_run. Optional; absent reads as true for planning chains. Every advice chain sets false: an advice call is never resumed, it is asked again (0.8.1 decided rule 6, P17).

summary.description: One line for a chain card in a list or a UI: what the council is, in at most 120 characters. Display only: no stage reads it, no prompt carries it, and it is left out of the stage cache's fingerprint, so editing it never makes a resumed run pay again. State what the chain is and how it is seated; never how well it works.

schemaVersion.description: v8 item (b), part 2. Optional; absence defaults to 1 (src/chain-lint.js reads and defaults it, does not require it). No schemaVersion-2 shape exists yet - this field buys the ABILITY to change the flag vocabulary later without silently misreading an old file, nothing more; no reader branches on its value today.

judging.description: "all-roles" (0.8.2, owner 7 Oct 2026, deliberate) waives chain-lint's mass-seat-votes and deep-dive-votes rules for this chain: every seat with another role (architects, proposers, the deep dive) also judges and votes, blind. Say so in "description".

selfReview.description: "allowed" waives chain-lint's self-review rule for this chain (a builder or reviser grading its own draft). Say why in "description".

panel.description: Absent means independent (blind) panel, the default. Only 'relay' is a real alternative chain.js reads.

estimate.description: Worst-case token estimate used by dry-run pricing only - never read by runChain's real behavior.

freedoms.description: Scoped debate freedoms (v7 item 3+4). Shape not re-validated here - engine-read, additive over time.

verify_post.description: v4 item 3: post-build re-invocation of runVerification. Same shape as verify.

preflight.description: v4 item 2 (task-description-only review pre-propose). Boolean or object with optional 'seats'.

ambiguity_union.description: Only "enabled" is read. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint (a typo like "enable" would otherwise silently skip the stage).

canary.description: Only "enabled" and "sampleRate" are read from a chain file. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint.

criteria_kinds.description: Criterion kinds (src/criteria-kinds.js): each criterion is checkable (with the command or measurement that settles it) or judgement. Only "enabled" is read. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint.

decisions.description: Only "enabled" is read. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint.

alternatives.description: Only "enabled", "maxTokens" and "debaters" are read. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint (a typo like "enable" would otherwise silently skip a paid stage). Who writes the architectures is seats.alternatives when set (tiered councils), else seats.proposers, else seats.critics.

debaters.description: Experimental (tiered councils). "authors" (the default): the authors post on each other's architectures. "all": seats.proposers (the mass seats) post on them too; only the authors reply.

answer_back.description: 0.8.2 (owner decision 3, 5 Oct 2026, ticket 10). With enabled true the harness builds, after each revise, what each judge will be shown in the next round about its own earlier objections (their ids, the reviser's declined reasons, the changed passages) and records a summary in report.json. Data only until the prompt that renders it is approved.

debate_hygiene.description: 0.8.2 (owner decision 2, 5 Oct 2026). shuffle: true gives every debate reader its own seeded order of the proposals and its own lab letters, and picks the canary target by seed (a pure function of the run id, so a resume replays it); the order each reader saw is recorded in report.json. noQuoteMarks: true marks, for the author, an objection or merge that quotes nothing of the proposal it is about. Both change what seats see; off in every chain written before them.

signoff_table.description: 0.8.2 (owner decision 1, 5 Oct 2026). With required true a judge's sign-off without a full per-criterion table (a row for every criterion, each with evidence and a verdict that says MET or FAILED) does not count: the seat is re-asked alone (once a round for a refused table; an unreadable reply keeps the existing two), then recorded as an abstention, never consent; heard clean verdicts are carried on an unchanged draft and the round cap still ends the loop. Changes when a run passes; off in every chain written before it existed.

majority_guard.description: Experimental (tiered councils). With enabled true: authors see each argument once with no lab letter and no count, the reply prompts carry an evidence bar, and a withdrawal that does not quote the argument it concedes to is recorded as unargued and the proposal stays for the builder to judge. Changes prompts; off in every chain written before it existed.

advise.description: Experimental (the council advisor, src/advise.js). With enabled true the chain answers one question with one leaning and the recorded dissent: the seats in seats.critics answer the brief blind, optionally read each other once (anonymised, no head-count) and keep or change their answer, and the harness rolls the answers up. It returns before every planning stage. usd is the call's own ceiling inside the run's cap and is required when enabled; the blind opinions are refused, with nothing called, when their worst case is above it.

rounds.description: Debate rounds after the blind opinions. Default 0. A round that moves no answer stops the debate.

skipDebateWhenUnanimous.description: Default true: no debate when every blind answer agrees.

synthesis.description: "none" (default): the harness rolls the answers up, no call. "seat": seats.builder, which must not be on the panel, writes the text of the leaning; the dissent is still the harness's.

samples.description: Default 1. Each seat is asked this many times, independently (a one-model-asked-k-times control arm). Not with rounds above 0.

max_wall_ms.description: Optional (since 0.8.2 no shipped chain sets it, and no chain must) wall-clock ceiling for the whole call, in milliseconds (brief 29). Every request gets it as its own deadline, and once it has passed no further call is started and the run ends at exit 18 with report-partial.json (stoppedBy wall_clock; 0.8.1). A call still running at the deadline is cut off and recorded as not answering. Was required for an advice chain in 0.8.1 (P17); optional since 0.8.2. Unset: no ceiling beyond the per-request default of 2 hours.

deep_dive.description: Experimental (tiered councils). One seat (seats.deep_dive), one job, a large output cap and its own dollar cap (usd, required when enabled) inside the run's cap. It reads the source in chunks, once per focus entry; its findings go to the reviser before the panel's first review. It does not vote.

handoff_contract.description: 0.8.2 (item 6b): settings for the harness-written "Before you build" and "Replan triggers" sections of HANDOFF.md. Two keys are read. "check_failures": how many times in a row a criterion's named check may fail before the builder is told to stop and replan. Default 2 (the number the harness's own stall rule treats as a stall: dispute.stall_rounds is at least 2). "milestones": see its own description.

milestones.description: Default false. When true the harness parses the handoff for seat-written milestones (src/milestones.js) and records what it finds: every criterion discharged by a milestone with a check, every check with an expected result. A finding never changes passed. The words that ask the handoff seat to write them are recorded in src/roles.js (the seven shipped planning chains set this).

argued.description: Opt-in "How this plan was argued" (ARGUED.md): a beginner-facing account of the debate, written on the handoff seat from the run's own record. Only "enabled" is read.

claims.description: v7 item 1 claim-extraction config. Engine-read, not re-validated here.

lints.description: Only "enabled" and "forks" are read. Unknown keys fail here and in chain-lint.

transport.description: Reserved for future transport-level config; not read by any shipped chain today.

challenge.description: src/chain-lint.js rule 6 already hard-validates this exhaustively (only 'enabled' is a real key) - this schema mirrors that exact shape rather than re-deriving it.

quorum.description: Opt-in quorum floor for unanimous sign-off (0.7.8): the panel's sign-off counts only when at least minHeard reviewers gave a verdict. Off when absent; no shipped chain sets it.

dispute.description: Dispute stage and its stall rule (src/chain.js, 2026-09-20). src/chain-lint.js rule 11b hard-validates this - only these two keys, stall_rounds at least 2, and signoff must be 'unanimous' - and this schema mirrors that shape. The stage runs once when a unanimous chain stops WITHOUT agreement, records the unresolved dissent at the top of the deliverable, and never re-opens the vote; that bound is hard-coded rather than configurable, same stance as challenge's one-round bound.

revise.description: Reviser output mode (src/patch-revise.js, 2026-09-20). Default 'full' (unchanged behaviour: the reviser rewrites the whole plan). 'patch' asks for search/replace blocks the harness applies locally, so text nobody objected to stays byte-identical by construction rather than by trust, and falls back to one full rewrite if any block does not apply cleanly. src/chain-lint.js rule 11c hard-validates it; whether real models produce reliably verbatim anchors is UNVERIFIED, which is why it ships default-off.

security_review.description: Final security-review gate (src/security-review.js). src/chain-lint.js rule 6c hard-validates it the same way as challenge (only 'enabled' is a real key; the blocking severities are fixed in code, not a chain setting) - this schema mirrors that exact shape. The reviewer seat itself lives under seats.security_reviewer.

allocator.description: src/chain-lint.js rule 7 already hard-validates tool names and keyword shape at runtime with better messages; this schema only pins the three known keys.

compliance.description: src/chain-lint.js rule 8 cross-checks these against real seat providers and the description text at runtime; this schema only pins the two known keys.

roster.description: src/chain-lint.js rule 9 already resolves criteria_seat against real seat labs at runtime; this schema only pins the two known keys.

criteria.description: Hand-written criteria, bypassing the criteria stage - see chains/gp-judge-*.json. An item may be an object carrying its kind (src/criteria-kinds.js).

seats.description: Keys validated against KNOWN_SEAT_KEYS by src/chain-lint.js rule 1 at runtime with a better error message (names the real unrecognized key); this schema only requires the value be an object so a typo'd top-level shape (an array, a string) is still caught here.
